# pulumi-docker-containers

The source for Pulumi's official Docker images.

**Pulumi IaC: infrastructure as code in any programming language.**

[Pulumi IaC](https://www.pulumi.com/product/infrastructure-as-code/) is an open-source infrastructure as code tool for creating, deploying, and managing cloud infrastructure on any cloud. Write your infrastructure in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, C#, Java, or YAML, and use the loops, functions, classes, testing tools, and package managers you already know.

The slim language images are much smaller than `pulumi/pulumi`, at 200 to 300 MB compared to about 2 GB.

Each image's README lists its tags, platforms, and language versions. The same README is published as the image's description on Docker Hub and the AWS ECR Public Gallery.

## Tags and platforms

Image tags match the version of the Pulumi CLI they contain, and `latest` points to the most recent release.

- `pulumi/pulumi` and `pulumi/pulumi-provider-build-environment` are built on Debian 13 (trixie) for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. `pulumi/pulumi` also has `-nonroot` tags that run as a `pulumi` user.
- The other images are built on two base images:
  - Debian 13 (trixie) slim, for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, tagged `-debian`. Tags without a suffix are the same image as the `-debian` tag.
  - [Red Hat UBI 9 minimal](https://hub.docker.com/r/redhat/ubi9-minimal), tagged `-ubi`. `pulumi/pulumi-base` is built for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, and the language images for `linux/amd64` only.

Images are published to [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/u/pulumi), the [AWS ECR Public Gallery](https://gallery.ecr.aws/pulumi/), and the [GitHub Container Registry](https://github.com/orgs/pulumi/packages?repo_name=pulumi-docker-containers).

## Language versions

Language versions follow the supported releases of each language. Images without a language version in their name use the default:

| Language | Default | Other versions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js | 26 | 22, 24 |
| Python | 3.13 | 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.14 |
| .NET | 8.0 | 9.0, 10.0 |
| Go | 1.26.10 | |
| Java (OpenJDK) | 21 | |

To choose a version in the slim images, use the image with that version in its name, for example `pulumi/pulumi-nodejs-22`. To choose a version in `pulumi/pulumi`, see [its README](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers/blob/main/docker/pulumi/README.md#choosing-a-language-version).

## Considerations

The base and language images _don't_ include extra tools you might need for a particular provider. For example, if you use the [Kubernetes provider](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-kubernetes) with [Helm](https://helm.sh/), use one of these images as the base for your own image and install `helm` there, or use `pulumi/pulumi`.

## Releases

Images are built and published automatically for every release of the [Pulumi CLI](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/releases), usually once a week, with patch releases in between when needed. Image tags match the version of the Pulumi CLI they contain. For example, when Pulumi `v3.200.0` is released, it's published as `3.200.0`. The `latest` tag always points to the most recent release.

To avoid unexpected upgrades, pin your image to a specific version tag rather than `latest`.

Images are scanned nightly for vulnerabilities. We remediate findings where we can, on a best-effort basis. Some findings, such as vulnerabilities in base images with no available fix, are outside our control.

## Getting help

- Problems with an image, such as a missing tool, a vulnerability, or a broken tag: [open an issue in pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers/issues/new).
- Problems with the Pulumi CLI or SDKs: [open an issue in pulumi/pulumi](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/issues/new/choose).
- Questions: ask in the [Pulumi Community Slack](https://slack.pulumi.com/).
